options.option_text: Timid (correct: audacious = bold/daring; timid = lacking confidence or courage ✓)

questions.explanation: B is correct. AUDACIOUS means showing a willingness to take bold risks; daring. Antonyms: timid, cowardly, meek, cautious. Synonyms: bold, daring, fearless, intrepid. Root: Latin audax = bold.

options.option_text: Talkative (synonym: verbose = using too many words)
Concise (correct: verbose = using more words than needed; concise = expressing ideas briefly ✓)

questions.explanation: C is correct. VERBOSE means using more words than necessary; long-winded. Antonyms: concise, succinct, terse, laconic, brief. Synonyms: wordy, prolix, long-winded, garrulous. Root: Latin verbum = word.

options.option_text: Alleviate (correct: exacerbate = make worse; alleviate = make less severe ✓)

questions.explanation: D is correct. EXACERBATE (verb): make a problem, bad situation, or negative feeling worse. Antonyms: alleviate, mitigate, ameliorate, relieve, ease. Synonyms: aggravate, worsen, intensify. Root: Latin exacerbare = to irritate/embitter.

options.option_text: Miserly (partial synonym — penurious also implies stinginess)
Affluent (correct: penurious = extremely poor/stingy; affluent = wealthy ✓)
Frugal (related but frugal is positive, penurious negative — not exact antonym)

questions.explanation: C is correct. PENURIOUS (adjective): extremely poor; unwilling to spend money. Antonyms: affluent, wealthy, opulent, generous. Synonyms: destitute, impoverished, indigent. Root: Latin penuria = want/poverty.

options.option_text: Faithful (correct: perfidious = guilty of betrayal; faithful = loyal and trustworthy ✓)

questions.explanation: B is correct. PERFIDIOUS (adjective): deceitful and untrustworthy; treacherous. Root: Latin perfidia = faithlessness (per + fides/faith). Antonyms: faithful, loyal, trustworthy, steadfast. Synonyms: treacherous, disloyal, duplicitous.

options.option_text: Critic (correct: sycophant = excessive flatterer who uses flattery to gain advantage; critic = one who expresses honest negative judgement ✓)
Supporter (not an antonym — supporters can be sincere)

questions.explanation: C is correct. SYCOPHANT (noun): a person who acts obsequiously toward someone important in order to gain advantage; a flatterer. Antonym: critic, detractor (one who speaks against). Synonyms: toady, yes-man, bootlicker, flatterer. Root: Greek sykophantēs = informer.

options.option_text: Permanent (correct: transient = not permanent; permanent = lasting for ever ✓)

questions.explanation: C is correct. TRANSIENT (adjective): lasting only for a short time; temporary. Antonyms: permanent, lasting, enduring, eternal, perpetual. Synonyms: fleeting, momentary, ephemeral, transitory. Root: Latin transire = to pass over.

options.option_text: Harmony (correct: cacophony = harsh mixture of sounds; harmony = pleasing combination of sounds ✓)

questions.explanation: C is correct. CACOPHONY (noun): a harsh, discordant mixture of sounds. Root: Greek kakos (bad) + phone (sound). Antonym: harmony, euphony (eu=good + phone=sound). Synonyms: discord, dissonance, din. Memory: caco=bad (cacophony/cacophonous) vs eu=good (euphony/euphonious).

options.option_text: Calm (synonym: placid = serenely free from disturbance)
Agitated (correct: placid = calm and peaceful; agitated = troubled/anxious ✓)

questions.explanation: C is correct. PLACID (adjective): not easily upset or excited; calm and peaceful. Antonyms: agitated, turbulent, excitable, restless, tempestuous. Synonyms: calm, serene, tranquil, peaceful. Memory: 'Placid lake' — calm surface vs stormy/agitated.

options.option_text: Assertive (correct: diffident = modest or shy due to lack of self-confidence; assertive = confident and self-assured ✓)
Aggressive (too extreme; the antonym should match the degree)

questions.explanation: C is correct. DIFFIDENT (adjective): modest or shy because of lack of self-confidence. Antonyms: assertive, confident, self-assured, bold. Synonyms: shy, timid, reserved, bashful. Root: Latin diffidere = to distrust (dis + fidere = trust). Exam trap: 'different' ≠ 'diffident'.

options.option_text: Destitute (synonym: indigent = without food, clothing, and other necessities)
Prosperous (correct: indigent = very poor; prosperous = successful, especially financially ✓)
Homeless (describes a condition of poverty, not opposite)

questions.explanation: C is correct. INDIGENT (adjective): extremely poor; needy. Antonyms: prosperous, affluent, wealthy, well-off. Synonyms: destitute, impoverished, penurious, needy. Root: Latin indigent = lacking (in + egere = to need). Exam context: 'indigent populations' in social welfare passages.

options.option_text: Petty (correct: magnanimous = generous in forgiving; petty = small-minded and ungenerous ✓)

questions.explanation: C is correct. MAGNANIMOUS (adjective): very generous or forgiving, especially toward a rival or less powerful person. Root: Latin magnus (great) + animus (mind/soul). Antonyms: petty, small-minded, vindictive, uncharitable. Synonyms: generous, noble, benevolent, charitable.
